chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn al-Muthanna) from Fadalah from Mu'awiya who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say about a person in ihram who kills a louse? He said: 'There is no penalty in the louse, and it is not appropriate that he intentionally kill it.'

Thus, there is no contradiction in these narrations with what we have previously stated, because they came in the context of concession (rukhsah). It is permissible that the intended meaning refers to the one who is bothered by it; for if the matter is so, it is permissible for him to do so, except that he is obliged to pay the ransom (kaffarah) as we have previously stated.

And his saying (peace be upon him) 'There is nothing upon him' means that if he does that, there is no penalty upon him, or there is no specific penalty upon him, as is obligatory upon him in the case of killing other things.
And there is no harm if the person in ihram throws the ticks off his camel, but he is not allowed to throw off the halamah (a specific type of tick or swelling). Narrated.

key_terms.الرُّخْصَةِ: Concession or dispensation in Islamic law
key_terms.الْحَلَمَةَ: A specific type of tick or swelling on the camel
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Ransom or expiation (penalty for breaking ihram rules)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: Person in ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in ihram who kills a louse?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that killing a louse (*qamalah*) incurs no specific penalty, interpreting the ruling as a concession (*rukhsah*) for those bothered by them, though some scholars argue a ransom is still due if done intentionally due to annoyance. The text further distinguishes the permissibility of removing ticks (*qurad*) from camels versus the specific prohibition of removing the *halamah* (a specific type of tick or worm), highlighting the nuanced application of *kaffarah* in Ihram rituals. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between minor pests where the penalty is waived or minimal versus larger creatures requiring full expiation.
